meanings.note: South Korea's national public broadcaster

examples.trans: A new drama is starting on KBS.
KBS broadcast review rules are strict.

meanings.note: formal evaluation of broadcast content, policies, or proposals

examples.trans: That song passed the broadcast review.
The review committee will decide.

meanings.note: often followed by -상 ('according to / under')

examples.trans: You have to follow company rules.
Under the rules, entry is prohibited here.

meanings.note: used for clothing, scenes, or jokes considered too provocative

examples.text: 이 옷은 방송에 입기에는 좀 야해요.
examples.trans: This outfit is a bit too revealing to wear on broadcast.
The racy scenes were edited out.
The outfit you're wearing today is really pretty.
It's cold, so please wear warm clothes.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 이것

examples.trans: How much is this?
This is really delicious.

meanings.note: placed directly before a verb or adjective for short-form negation

examples.trans: I'm not going to school today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

되다.gloss: to become; to work, be allowed

meanings.en: to be allowed, to work, to be okay
meanings.note: 안 되다 means 'not allowed' or 'won't do'
with -이/가

examples.trans: You're not allowed to take photos here.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.note: negative copula; takes -이/가 on the negated noun

examples.trans: I am not a student.
That's not my fault.

meanings.note: colloquially often pronounced/written 이쁘다

examples.trans: The flowers are really pretty.
This color is prettier.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: auxiliary negation verb used after -지

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold.
I won't be late today.

meanings.en: see, told you so, look at that
meanings.note: contracted from 그거 보다 ('look at that'); commonly used as 거봐 or 거봐요

examples.trans: See, I was right, wasn't I?
Told you so, it's raining.

meanings.note: from English 'PD'; commonly addressed with -님 as 피디님

examples.trans: PD, filming preparations are all done.
That variety show PD is very famous.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: long-running weekly live K-pop music program on KBS2

examples.trans: Cindy is appearing on Music Bank today.
I watch Music Bank every Friday.

meanings.note: affectionate/informal word for mother

examples.trans: I went to the market with my mum.
The food my mum makes is the most delicious.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch, to look

meanings.en: to see, to watch, to look

meanings.note: as an auxiliary verb after -아/어

examples.trans: I watched an interesting movie yesterday.
Take a look at this photo.

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have; to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be present, to have
meanings.note: used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 ('have ever done')

meanings.en: to stay, to remain in a state
meanings.note: as an auxiliary after -아/어 (e.g., 나가 있다 'to be outside')

examples.trans: If you have time, let's drink coffee together.
Step outside for just a moment.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: bound noun; -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 means 'it seems that / I think'

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.
What I like is music.

meanings.note: in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 ('it seems / I think')

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: with -와/과 or -처럼

examples.trans: You seem a bit tired today.
I think we have the same idea.

meanings.note: humble 1st-person singular pronoun used in polite speech

examples.trans: My name is Baek Seung-chan.
I'll head out first.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.trans: This book is really interesting.
Is there a cafe near here?

meanings.note: colloquial clipping of 프로그램
clipping of 프로페셔널

examples.trans: What shows are you watching these days?
That show has high viewership ratings.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to participate in

examples.trans: What are you going to do on the weekend?
I won't do this job.
Today I'll just stay at home.
Don't just walk past, say hello.

meanings.en: to go, to leave, to head

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
You can't leave now.

meanings.note: also used as a noun meaning 'the real thing'

examples.trans: It's really hot today.
Is that really true?

meanings.note: 다 ('all') + plural suffix -들

examples.trans: Has everyone been doing well?
Everyone, please be quiet for a moment.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.

meanings.note: 다음에 means 'next time'

examples.trans: Let's eat together next time.
We have to get off at the next station.
See you again tomorrow!
It started raining again.
I'm going to meet a friend on the weekend.
Let's meet again next week.
